cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Choose What Matters More
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. They're calling your audition number. Do you want the part enough to let them hear you? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want it. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I can walk you in or drive you home. Which want am I helping?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can promise I'll stay. Is that enough to risk the audition, or are we going home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're calling your audition number. Do you want the part enough to let them hear you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want it. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can walk you in or drive you home. Which want am I helping?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can promise I'll stay. Is that enough to risk the audition, or are we going home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we renew this lease, do you want my honest answer about living together or a peaceful dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your honest answer. Just don't say anything that makes me panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't promise both. Shall I answer, or shall we order?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Answer. But start by saying we're fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the answer you're choosing for me. Do you still want mine?

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I haven't booked our anniversary trip. Can you hear why before you get your laptop? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you just needed help with the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the laptop shut. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Can you still sit beside me while I explain?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You've locked the shop. You can stop doing the cheerful voice for me. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't owe me a second performance. Can we lock the stockroom and let you be upset out here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've locked the shop. You can stop doing the cheerful voice for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't owe me a second performance. Can we lock the stockroom and let you be upset out here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over dinner you keep saying you're managing. What's hard about going home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The silence. I leave the television on so it sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask me over instead of pretending you've got company?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you invite me without that promise? I'd like to come even if you're miserable and we eat toast.

cards.title: I Started the Spiral
cards.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Let's reassure the stallholders that the fair is still on. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You panicked about the forecast and told them to cancel their vans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then I have the right contact list. I'll say the arrangements are unchanged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their arrangements changed because of you. Two vans are cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find replacements. Could your update call it a transport hiccup? They need something calm to read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's reassure the stallholders that the fair is still on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You panicked about the forecast and told them to cancel their vans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I have the right contact list. I'll say the arrangements are unchanged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their arrangements changed because of you. Two vans are cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find replacements. Could your update call it a transport hiccup? They need something calm to read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club money's in the other envelope. Let's tell everyone they can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You phoned me crying that the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're the first person I'm reassuring. Could you pass on that it's all accounted for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told the whole committee what you said.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll ring them together. Could you introduce it as a routine balance update? No need to replay the tears.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before I open the scholarship letter, do we have clean teaspoons? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made your tea. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You've put sugar in mine. I'll need another cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we swap cups, how will you know which has sugar? We need labels before anything gets mixed up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I open the scholarship letter, do we have clean teaspoons?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made your tea. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put sugar in mine. I'll need another cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we swap cups, how will you know which has sugar? We need labels before anything gets mixed up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss me moving out, can you check my train time again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six twelve. I've checked five times, and your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Does this ticket work at the barrier, or do I need the booking email?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through the barrier. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you're coming onto the platform, we need to check whether you need a ticket too.

beats.text: Six twelve. I've checked five times, and your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Does this ticket work at the barrier, or do I need the booking email?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through the barrier. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you're coming onto the platform, we need to check whether you need a ticket too.
